question: Ecological succession is defined as:

options.text: process by which geological changes take place
process by which the mix of species and habitat in an area changes over time
process by which the many species get extinct

solution:
The correct answer is "__**process by which the mix of species and habitat in an area changes over time**__". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ecological succession**__ is defined as t__**he process by which the mix of species and habitat in an area changes over time**__.

 __
 
• The mechanism through which a** region's species** and habitat mix **evolve** throughout time is called** ecological succession**.
 
• These species eventually replace each other until a "**climax community**" is attained, such as a full forest, or until a **disruption**, such as a fire, happens.
 
• Or we can say that ecological succession is the process by which a biological community's **composition changes** as time passes.
 
• **Primary** and **secondary** succession has been identified as two distinct forms. In situations where the** soil** is **unable **to support life due to reasons like lava flows, recently formed sand dunes, or boulders left behind by a receding glacier, **primary succession** takes place.
 
• **Secondary succession** happens in places where an earlier **community** has been **eliminated**; it is characterized by relatively small disruptions that do not completely wipe out the environment's life and nutrition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 __**Process**__
 __**Description**__
 
 

 **Process of ecological changes**
 Events known as **geological processes** take place over a period of time that can range from millions of years to thousands of kilometers.
 
 

 **Process of deforestation**
 When people **clear** or thin **forests** to make lumber or to use the land where the trees once stood for farming, grazing, extraction (of minerals, oil, or gas), or development as a result of population growth and migration, this is known as **deforestation**.
 
 

 **Process of extinction of species**
 A **species** goes extinct when it **disappears** from the planet. When a species' population declines as a result of environmental factors such as habitat fragmentation, climate change, natural disasters, etc. The** dinosaur** is among the most well-known instances of an **extinct species**.
